principle: All non-text elements (images, videos, audio, charts, interactives, maps) must follow these layout rules to prevent misalignment and overlap with text content.
container_structure:
Text content first (

), then the visual element in its own container (

...), then the next text content. Never place images/videos directly adjacent to

tags without a wrapper div.
css_requirements_for_visual_containers: margin: 2rem 0 — vertical spacing above and below to separate from text
display: block — force block layout, never inline
images/videos: max-width: 100%; height: auto; display: block; margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto — center and prevent overflow
charts: width: 100%; max-width: 720px; margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto — constrain width and center
full-width elements (teaser, hero): width: 100vw; margin-left: calc(50% - 50vw); margin-right: calc(50% - 50vw); max-width: none (or a separate wrapper). Do not rely on old left: 50% breakout hacks.

aspect_orientation_sizing._why: A WIDTH cap alone (the rule below) sizes a portrait/standard image correctly but mis-sizes a LANDSCAPE or PANORAMA shot: a 3.19:1 stadium photo capped only on width renders as a thin full-width strip (~175px tall — the gold-blog bug), and an uncapped tall image can tower past the screen. So every in-body image is bounded on BOTH axes, matched to its intrinsic aspect: a width cap AND a height band / max-height ceiling, with a dual-bound belt-and-suspenders so neither axis runs away.
aspect_orientation_sizing.orientation_classes: Class each in-body
aspect_orientation_sizing.dual_bound_rule: Always set BOTH a max-width AND (for is-landscape/is-pano) a height band / max-height. The width cap stops column overflow (the existing rule); the height band stops the thin-strip / towering failure. The orientation class MUST match the asset's real aspect — `is-portrait` on a 3:1 image (or `is-pano` on a tall image) is a misclassing bug. Pair with the auditor `check_12` (asserts both bounds + the orientation/aspect match) and the validate.py §11 note below.
aspect_orientation_sizing.validate_py_note: inspector/scripts/validate.py §11 (`image_no_maxwidth_cap`) is extended from 'has a max-width' to ALSO assert, for a wide/pano in-body

specific_element_rules.images: wrap in
specific_element_rules.videos: wrap in <div class="video-container"> with margin: 2rem 0, apply max-width: 100% to the <video>.
specific_element_rules.generated_audio: wrap in <div class="audio-container"> with margin: 2rem 0, include a title/caption, visible controls, and a muted visual fallback.
specific_element_rules.charts_vega_lite: container div with margin: 2rem auto, set "width": "container" in the Vega spec.
specific_element_rules.interactive_elements: wrap in <div class="interactive-container"> with margin: 2rem 0, all controls inside this container.

prevent_common_bugs:
Never place images/videos directly adjacent to

tags without a wrapper div.
Never use float on visual elements — use margin: auto for centering instead.
Always set explicit height for map containers (Leaflet requires it).
For responsive images: width: 100%; height: auto; max-width: [original-width]px.
Test that text never wraps around or overlaps visual elements.
teaser_exception: The teaser is full-viewport and appears before the headline — it does NOT follow the 720px content-width constraint. Use width: 100vw; margin-left: calc(50% - 50vw); margin-right: calc(50% - 50vw); max-width: none; height: 100vh to break out. If the teaser lives inside a figure or visual wrapper, clear any inherited max-width there too.
base_layout: Max content width: 720px, centered. Charts and teasers may break out to full width.
Georgia or system-serif for body text, system-ui for labels and UI elements.
Responsive, no horizontal scroll on mobile.
